title: Aggregate Functions & Statistical Calculations
description: Compute summary statistics with COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, and PostgreSQL's FILTER clause.

data.text: Aggregate functions compute a single summary value across a collection of rows. Common functions include `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `STRING_AGG`, and `JSONB_AGG`.

rows: Counts all rows in the group regardless of contents.
Counts only rows where specified column is NOT NULL.

data.text: SQL:2003 introduced the `FILTER (WHERE condition)` clause for aggregate functions. PostgreSQL implements this cleanly, eliminating messy `CASE WHEN` statements when computing conditional metrics.

data.title: Conditional Aggregates with FILTER
data.content: Computing multiple metrics in a single pass over the table.
data.code:
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue,
    -- Using FILTER instead of clumsy SUM(CASE WHEN ...)
    SUM(total_amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'PAID') AS paid_revenue,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'REFUNDED') AS refunded_orders_count,
    ROUND(AVG(total_amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'PAID'), 2) AS avg_paid_order_value
FROM orders;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `FILTER (WHERE condition)` for clean, performant conditional aggregations.
Aggregate functions can be combined with `STRING_AGG` and `JSONB_AGG` to group values into arrays.
